title: Ephesus: the sons of Sceva + the silversmiths' riot for Artemis (Diana)

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper country came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples:
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν Ἀπολλῶ εἶναι ἐν Κορίνθῳ Παῦλον διελθόντα τὰ ἀνωτερικὰ μέρη ἐλθεῖν εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εὑρεῖν τινας μαθητάς,
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en tō ton Apollō einai en Korinthō Paulon dielthonta ta anōterika merē elthein eis Epheson kai heurein tinas mathētas,

paragraphs.text: and he said unto them, Did ye receive the Holy Spirit when ye believed? And they [said] unto him, Nay, we did not so much as hear whether the Holy Spirit was [given].
paragraphs.original: εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Εἰ πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐλάβετε πιστεύσαντες; οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀλλʼ οὐδʼ εἰ πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἔστιν ἠκούσαμεν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen te pros autous· Ei pneuma hagion elabete pisteusantes; hoi de pros auton· Allʼ oudʼ ei pneuma hagion estin ēkousamen.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Into what then were ye baptized? And they said, Into John`s baptism.
paragraphs.original: εἶπέν τε· Εἰς τί οὖν ἐβαπτίσθητε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Εἰς τὸ Ἰωάννου βάπτισμα.
paragraphs.translit: eipen te· Eis ti oun ebaptisthēte; hoi de eipan· Eis to Iōannou baptisma.

paragraphs.text: And Paul said, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people that they should believe on him that should come after him, that is, on Jesus.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ Παῦλος· Ἰωάννης ἐβάπτισεν βάπτισμα μετανοίας, τῷ λαῷ λέγων εἰς τὸν ἐρχόμενον μετʼ αὐτὸν ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de Paulos· Iōannēs ebaptisen baptisma metanoias, tō laō legōn eis ton erchomenon metʼ auton hina pisteusōsin, toutʼ estin eis ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: And when they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἐβαπτίσθησαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: akousantes de ebaptisthēsan eis to onoma tou kyriou Iēsou·

paragraphs.text: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπιθέντος αὐτοῖς τοῦ Παύλου χεῖρας ἦλθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπʼ αὐτούς, ἐλάλουν τε γλώσσαις καὶ ἐπροφήτευον.
paragraphs.translit: kai epithentos autois tou Paulou cheiras ēlthe to pneuma to hagion epʼ autous, elaloun te glōssais kai eprophēteuon.

paragraphs.text: And they were in all about twelve men.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δὲ οἱ πάντες ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ δώδεκα.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de hoi pantes andres hōsei dōdeka.

paragraphs.text: And he entered into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, reasoning and persuading [as to] the things concerning the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: Εἰσελθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ἐπαρρησιάζετο ἐπὶ μῆνας τρεῖς διαλεγόμενος καὶ πείθων περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Eiselthōn de eis tēn synagōgēn eparrēsiazeto epi mēnas treis dialegomenos kai peithōn peri tēs basileias tou theou.

paragraphs.text: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δέ τινες ἐσκληρύνοντο καὶ ἠπείθουν κακολογοῦντες τὴν ὁδὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πλήθους, ἀποστὰς ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀφώρισεν τοὺς μαθητάς, καθʼ ἡμέραν διαλεγόμενος ἐν τῇ σχολῇ Τυράννου.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de tines esklērynonto kai ēpeithoun kakologountes tēn hodon enōpion tou plēthous, apostas apʼ autōn aphōrisen tous mathētas, kathʼ hēmeran dialegomenos en tē scholē Tyrannou.

paragraphs.text: And this continued for the space of two years; so that all they that dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ ἔτη δύο, ὥστε πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας τὴν Ἀσίαν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας.
paragraphs.translit: touto de egeneto epi etē dyo, hōste pantas tous katoikountas tēn Asian akousai ton logon tou kyriou, Ioudaious te kai Hellēnas.

paragraphs.text: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
paragraphs.original: Δυνάμεις τε οὐ τὰς τυχούσας ὁ θεὸς ἐποίει διὰ τῶν χειρῶν Παύλου,
paragraphs.translit: Dynameis te ou tas tychousas ho theos epoiei dia tōn cheirōn Paulou,

paragraphs.text: insomuch that unto the sick were carried away from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the evil spirits went out.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας ἀποφέρεσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ σουδάρια ἢ σιμικίνθια καὶ ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι ἀπʼ αὐτῶν τὰς νόσους, τά τε πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκπορεύεσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: hōste kai epi tous asthenountas apopheresthai apo tou chrōtos autou soudaria ē simikinthia kai apallassesthai apʼ autōn tas nosous, ta te pneumata ta ponēra ekporeuesthai.

paragraphs.text: But certain also of the strolling Jews, exorcists, took upon them to name over them that had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
paragraphs.original: ἐπεχείρησαν δέ τινες καὶ τῶν περιερχομένων Ἰουδαίων ἐξορκιστῶν ὀνομάζειν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες· Ὁρκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν Παῦλος κηρύσσει.
paragraphs.translit: epecheirēsan de tines kai tōn perierchomenōn Ioudaiōn exorkistōn onomazein epi tous echontas ta pneumata ta ponēra to onoma tou kyriou Iēsou legontes· Horkizō hymas ton Iēsoun hon Paulos kēryssei.

paragraphs.text: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, a chief priest, who did this.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δέ τινος Σκευᾶ Ἰουδαίου ἀρχιερέως ἑπτὰ υἱοὶ τοῦτο ποιοῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de tinos Skeua Ioudaiou archiereōs hepta hyioi touto poiountes.

paragraphs.text: And the evil spirit answered and said unto them, Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are ye?
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθὲν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸν Ἰησοῦν γινώσκω καὶ τὸν Παῦλον ἐπίσταμαι, ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνες ἐστέ;
paragraphs.translit: apokrithen de to pneuma to ponēron eipen autois· Ton Iēsoun ginōskō kai ton Paulon epistamai, hymeis de tines este;

paragraphs.text: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and mastered both of them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐφαλόμενος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ἐν ᾧ ἦν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν κατακυριεύσας ἀμφοτέρων ἴσχυσεν κατʼ αὐτῶν, ὥστε γυμνοὺς καὶ τετραυματισμένους ἐκφυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου ἐκείνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ephalomenos ho anthrōpos epʼ autous en hō ēn to pneuma to ponēron katakyrieusas amphoterōn ischysen katʼ autōn, hōste gymnous kai tetraumatismenous ekphygein ek tou oikou ekeinou.

paragraphs.text: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, that dwelt at Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο γνωστὸν πᾶσιν Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν τὴν Ἔφεσον, καὶ ἐπέπεσεν φόβος ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς, καὶ ἐμεγαλύνετο τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: touto de egeneto gnōston pasin Ioudaiois te kai Hellēsin tois katoikousin tēn Epheson, kai epepesen phobos epi pantas autous, kai emegalyneto to onoma tou kyriou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: Many also of them that had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.
paragraphs.original: πολλοί τε τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἤρχοντο ἐξομολογούμενοι καὶ ἀναγγέλλοντες τὰς πράξεις αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: polloi te tōn pepisteukotōn ērchonto exomologoumenoi kai anangellontes tas praxeis autōn.

paragraphs.text: And not a few of them that practised magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all; and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
paragraphs.original: ἱκανοὶ δὲ τῶν τὰ περίεργα πραξάντων συνενέγκαντες τὰς βίβλους κατέκαιον ἐνώπιον πάντων· καὶ συνεψήφισαν τὰς τιμὰς αὐτῶν καὶ εὗρον ἀργυρίου μυριάδας πέντε.
paragraphs.translit: hikanoi de tōn ta perierga praxantōn synenenkantes tas biblous katekaion enōpion pantōn· kai synepsēphisan tas timas autōn kai heuron argyriou myriadas pente.

paragraphs.text: So mightily grew the word of the Lord and prevailed.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως κατὰ κράτος τοῦ κυρίου ὁ λόγος ηὔξανεν καὶ ἴσχυεν.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kata kratos tou kyriou ho logos ēuxanen kai ischyen.

paragraphs.text: Now after these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληρώθη ταῦτα, ἔθετο ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῷ πνεύματι διελθὼν τὴν Μακεδονίαν καὶ Ἀχαΐαν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, εἰπὼν ὅτι Μετὰ τὸ γενέσθαι με ἐκεῖ δεῖ με καὶ Ῥώμην ἰδεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de eplērōthē tauta, etheto ho Paulos en tō pneumati dielthōn tēn Makedonian kai Achaian poreuesthai eis Hierosolyma, eipōn hoti Meta to genesthai me ekei dei me kai Rhōmēn idein.

paragraphs.text: And having sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
paragraphs.original: ἀποστείλας δὲ εἰς τὴν Μακεδονίαν δύο τῶν διακονούντων αὐτῷ, Τιμόθεον καὶ Ἔραστον, αὐτὸς ἐπέσχεν χρόνον εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν.
paragraphs.translit: aposteilas de eis tēn Makedonian dyo tōn diakonountōn autō, Timotheon kai Eraston, autos epeschen chronon eis tēn Asian.

paragraphs.text: And about that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν ἐκεῖνον τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de kata ton kairon ekeinon tarachos ouk oligos peri tēs hodou.

paragraphs.text: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Diana, brought no little business unto the craftsmen;
paragraphs.original: Δημήτριος γάρ τις ὀνόματι, ἀργυροκόπος, ποιῶν ναοὺς ἀργυροῦς Ἀρτέμιδος παρείχετο τοῖς τεχνίταις οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐργασίαν,
paragraphs.translit: Dēmētrios gar tis onomati, argyrokopos, poiōn naous argyrous Artemidos pareicheto tois technitais ouk oligēn ergasian,

paragraphs.text: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this business we have our wealth.
paragraphs.original: οὓς συναθροίσας καὶ τοὺς περὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργάτας εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες, ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἐκ ταύτης τῆς ἐργασίας ἡ εὐπορία ἡμῖν ἐστιν,
paragraphs.translit: hous synathroisas kai tous peri ta toiauta ergatas eipen· Andres, epistasthe hoti ek tautēs tēs ergasias hē euporia hēmin estin,

paragraphs.text: And ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands:
paragraphs.original: καὶ θεωρεῖτε καὶ ἀκούετε ὅτι οὐ μόνον Ἐφέσου ἀλλὰ σχεδὸν πάσης τῆς Ἀσίας ὁ Παῦλος οὗτος πείσας μετέστησεν ἱκανὸν ὄχλον, λέγων ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοὶ οἱ διὰ χειρῶν γινόμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: kai theōreite kai akouete hoti ou monon Ephesou alla schedon pasēs tēs Asias ho Paulos houtos peisas metestēsen hikanon ochlon, legōn hoti ouk eisin theoi hoi dia cheirōn ginomenoi.

paragraphs.text: and not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana be made of no account, and that she should even be deposed from her magnificence whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
paragraphs.original: οὐ μόνον δὲ τοῦτο κινδυνεύει ἡμῖν τὸ μέρος εἰς ἀπελεγμὸν ἐλθεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ τῆς μεγάλης θεᾶς Ἀρτέμιδος ἱερὸν εἰς οὐθὲν λογισθῆναι, μέλλειν τε καὶ καθαιρεῖσθαι τῆς μεγαλειότητος αὐτῆς, ἣν ὅλη ἡ Ἀσία καὶ ἡ οἰκουμένη σέβεται.
paragraphs.translit: ou monon de touto kindyneuei hēmin to meros eis apelegmon elthein, alla kai to tēs megalēs theas Artemidos hieron eis outhen logisthēnai, mellein te kai kathaireisthai tēs megaleiotētos autēs, hēn holē hē Asia kai hē oikoumenē sebetai.

paragraphs.text: And when they heard this they were filled with wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesus.
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ καὶ γενόμενοι πλήρεις θυμοῦ ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
paragraphs.translit: Akousantes de kai genomenoi plēreis thymou ekrazon legontes· Megalē hē Artemis Ephesiōn.

paragraphs.text: And the city was filled with the confusion: and they rushed with one accord into the theatre, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul`s companions in travel.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ πόλις τῆς συγχύσεως, ὥρμησάν τε ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον συναρπάσαντες Γάϊον καὶ Ἀρίσταρχον Μακεδόνας, συνεκδήμους Παύλου.
paragraphs.translit: kai eplēsthē hē polis tēs synchyseōs, hōrmēsan te homothymadon eis to theatron synarpasantes Gaion kai Aristarchon Makedonas, synekdēmous Paulou.

paragraphs.text: And when Paul was minded to enter in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
paragraphs.original: Παύλου δὲ βουλομένου εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον οὐκ εἴων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταί·
paragraphs.translit: Paulou de boulomenou eiselthein eis ton dēmon ouk eiōn auton hoi mathētai·

paragraphs.text: And certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent unto him and besought him not to adventure himself into the theatre.
paragraphs.original: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἀσιαρχῶν, ὄντες αὐτῷ φίλοι, πέμψαντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παρεκάλουν μὴ δοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον.
paragraphs.translit: tines de kai tōn Asiarchōn, ontes autō philoi, pempsantes pros auton parekaloun mē dounai heauton eis to theatron.

paragraphs.text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was in confusion; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
paragraphs.original: ἄλλοι μὲν οὖν ἄλλο τι ἔκραζον, ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἐκκλησία συγκεχυμένη, καὶ οἱ πλείους οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τίνος ἕνεκα συνεληλύθεισαν.
paragraphs.translit: alloi men oun allo ti ekrazon, ēn gar hē ekklēsia synkechymenē, kai hoi pleious ouk ēdeisan tinos heneka synelēlytheisan.

paragraphs.text: And they brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made a defense unto the people.
paragraphs.original: ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ὄχλου συνεβίβασαν Ἀλέξανδρον προβαλόντων αὐτὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὁ δὲ Ἀλέξανδρος κατασείσας τὴν χεῖρα ἤθελεν ἀπολογεῖσθαι τῷ δήμῳ.
paragraphs.translit: ek de tou ochlou synebibasan Alexandron probalontōn auton tōn Ioudaiōn, ho de Alexandros kataseisas tēn cheira ēthelen apologeisthai tō dēmō.

paragraphs.text: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν φωνὴ ἐγένετο μία ἐκ πάντων ὡς ἐπὶ ὥρας δύο κραζόντων· Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
paragraphs.translit: epignontes de hoti Ioudaios estin phōnē egeneto mia ek pantōn hōs epi hōras dyo krazontōn· Megalē hē Artemis Ephesiōn.

paragraphs.text: And when the townclerk had quieted the multitude, he saith, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there who knoweth not that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great Diana, and of the [image] which fell down from Jupiter?
paragraphs.original: καταστείλας δὲ ὁ γραμματεὺς τὸν ὄχλον φησίν· Ἄνδρες Ἐφέσιοι, τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἀνθρώπων ὃς οὐ γινώσκει τὴν Ἐφεσίων πόλιν νεωκόρον οὖσαν τῆς μεγάλης Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τοῦ διοπετοῦς;
paragraphs.translit: katasteilas de ho grammateus ton ochlon phēsin· Andres Ephesioi, tis gar estin anthrōpōn hos ou ginōskei tēn Ephesiōn polin neōkoron ousan tēs megalēs Artemidos kai tou diopetous;

paragraphs.text: Seeing then that these things cannot be gainsaid, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.
paragraphs.original: ἀναντιρρήτων οὖν ὄντων τούτων δέον ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς κατεσταλμένους ὑπάρχειν καὶ μηδὲν προπετὲς πράσσειν.
paragraphs.translit: anantirrētōn oun ontōn toutōn deon estin hymas katestalmenous hyparchein kai mēden propetes prassein.

paragraphs.text: For ye have brought [hither] these men, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess.
paragraphs.original: ἠγάγετε γὰρ τοὺς ἄνδρας τούτους οὔτε ἱεροσύλους οὔτε βλασφημοῦντας τὴν θεὸν ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ēgagete gar tous andras toutous oute hierosylous oute blasphēmountas tēn theon hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: If therefore Demetrius, and the craftsmen that are with him, have a matter against any man, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls: let them accuse one another.
paragraphs.original: εἰ μὲν οὖν Δημήτριος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ τεχνῖται ἔχουσιν πρός τινα λόγον, ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται καὶ ἀνθύπατοί εἰσιν, ἐγκαλείτωσαν ἀλλήλοις.
paragraphs.translit: ei men oun Dēmētrios kai hoi syn autō technitai echousin pros tina logon, agoraioi agontai kai anthypatoi eisin, enkaleitōsan allēlois.

paragraphs.text: But if ye seek anything about other matters, it shall be settled in the regular assembly.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δέ τι περαιτέρω ἐπιζητεῖτε, ἐν τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐπιλυθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ti peraiterō epizēteite, en tē ennomō ekklēsia epilythēsetai.

paragraphs.text: For indeed we are in danger to be accused concerning this day`s riot, there being no cause [for it]: and as touching it we shall not be able to give account of this concourse.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ κινδυνεύομεν ἐγκαλεῖσθαι στάσεως περὶ τῆς σήμερον μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος περὶ οὗ οὐ δυνησόμεθα ἀποδοῦναι λόγον περὶ τῆς συστροφῆς ταύτης. καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar kindyneuomen enkaleisthai staseōs peri tēs sēmeron mēdenos aitiou hyparchontos peri hou ou dynēsometha apodounai logon peri tēs systrophēs tautēs. kai tauta eipōn apelysen tēn ekklēsian.

paragraphs.text: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
